newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan revises timetable to join WTO.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan revises timetable to join WTO.

text.p: Taiwan on Wednesday revised its timetable to join the World Trade Organization, postponing its July goal to the end of 1997, after rival China insisted that it enter the world trade body before Taipei does.

"We may have difficulty in gaining WTO membership in July due to the slow progress of the Chinese communists in becoming a WTO member," vice economics minister Sheu Ke-sheng was quoted as saying by state-funded Central News Agency.
Sheu acknowledged to legislators during a parliament meeting that it is unlikely Taiwan will join the WTO before China.
WTO members have reached a consensus that the two sides of the Taiwan Strait could join the organisation at the same time.
China on Wednesday shrugged off a U.S. suggestion that Taiwan's entrance into the WTO should be independent of China's.
"We reiterate...our principle that China must join the WTO before Taiwan," said a spokesman of the Chinese Ministry of Foreign Trade and Economic Cooperation.

In Washington, U.S. Trade Representative Charlene Barshefsky said the United States believes Taiwan's accession to the WTO should be independent of China and should be based on commercial, not political, criteria.
China, which has viewed Taiwan as a rebel-held province after a civil war split them in 1949, has said Taiwan is a local territory with no rights to participate in international affairs.
Sheu said: "No one can be 100 percent sure when the Chinese communists would become a WTO member."
He said Taiwan should be able to complete talks with all 26 WTO members before July, but it is not up to the island to decide when exactly it may join the WTO.
He said Taiwan still needs to go through review meetings by the WTO headquarters in Geneva.
